findings.message: list 'table' is tested with 'in' inside a loop at depth 1 — CPython's list membership is an O(n) linear scan, so re-testing per outer iteration is O(n²); building a set/dict lookup or iterating directly is a candidate optimization

findings.message: list 'data' is indexed by loop variable 'i' at depth 1 — CPython's list subscript is O(1) per access, but a scan over the whole list re-walks it per outer iteration (O(n²)); iterating directly, using `enumerate`, or building a set/dict lookup is a candidate optimization

findings.message: list 'data' is scanned with `.index()` inside a loop at depth 1 — CPython's list `.index()` is an O(n) linear scan, so re-scanning per outer iteration is O(n²); building a set/dict lookup or a positional map is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'conn.execute' issues a db round-trip every iteration at loop depth 1 — the N+1 pattern (one query/request per element); batching into a single `IN (...)`, JOIN, or bulk request is a candidate optimization

findings.message: string 's' is accumulated with '+=' inside a loop at depth 1 — CPython strings are immutable, so each pass allocates a new string and copies both operands (O(n²)); accumulating pieces in a list and calling `str.join` once is a candidate optimization
findings.title: String accumulation in loop

findings.message: 'walk_down' calls itself directly at 1 site(s) — each recursive frame costs a CPython call and risks `RecursionError` at the interpreter recursion limit; converting to iteration or memoizing is a candidate optimization
findings.title: Direct recursion

findings.message: 'branchy' branches 17 ways (threshold 15) — complex control flow hides hot paths and resists testing; extracting helpers or table-driving the dispatch is a candidate optimization
findings.title: High cyclomatic complexity

findings.message: loops nest 3 deep here (chain reaches depth 3) — CPython runs an interpreted loop body per element, so an O(n^k) nest is the primary hotspot zone; flattening the nesting or using itertools early-exit helpers is a candidate optimization

findings.message: `range(len(...))` at loop depth 1 indexes the sequence by position and re-runs `len` each pass — iterating the sequence directly or using `enumerate` is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'dict' constructs a fresh value on every iteration at loop depth 1 — CPython allocates a new object header and backing store each pass (and deallocates it on rebind); hoisting the loop-invariant construction is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'list' called with a non-literal iterable every iteration at loop depth 1 — CPython eagerly allocates and copies the whole sequence, defeating lazy iteration; keeping the lazy generator (or hoisting) is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'pkg/cycle_b.py' and 'pkg/cycle_a.py' import each other, forming a cycle — CPython executes a partially-initialised module during the cycle, and the coupling resists testing; breaking the lowest-sorted edge into a shared leaf module is a candidate optimization

findings.message: directory '.' aggregates complexity 111 across 60 function(s) — the hottest component in this scan (thresholds are conservative and not yet measured on Python); splitting or simplifying its hottest functions is a candidate optimization

findings.message: loop body appends to list 'out' as its only statement at loop depth 1 — a list comprehension compiles to a specialised `LIST_APPEND` with inline iteration, avoiding the loop branch and per-element method lookup; rewriting it as a comprehension is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor' is constructed every iteration at loop depth 1 — CPython spawns worker threads/processes or allocates a new event loop (selector + self-pipe) each pass, never amortising the setup; creating the executor once outside the loop is a candidate optimization

findings.message: a `try`/`except` sits inside a loop body at depth 1 — CPython sets up exception-handling state for the block, so per-iteration `try` adds work on the hot path (the zero-cost-`try` optimization is version-dependent: CPython ≥ 3.11). Hoisting the `try` out of the loop or narrowing it is a candidate optimization
findings.title: `try`/`except` inside a loop

findings.message: 'deepcopy' copies a whole container every iteration at loop depth 1 — CPython allocates and fills a new object (`deepcopy` also walks the graph with a memo dict); copying once outside the loop or reusing the buffer is a candidate optimization
findings.title: Container copy inside loop

findings.message: 'df.iterrows' iterates row by row — pandas materialises a Python object per row (`iterrows` builds a `Series` with dtype coercion), so the per-row overhead dwarfs the vectorised work; column arithmetic or `groupby`/`itertuples`-free vectorisation is a candidate optimization

findings.message: 'pandas.concat' rebuilds the whole DataFrame every iteration at loop depth 1 — pandas copies the full frame on each `concat`/`append` (O(n²)); collecting rows in a list and concatenating once after the loop is a candidate optimization
